 High surf advisory in effect for north shores of Maui, Big Island
 By Star-Advertiser staff
 Nov. 16, 2026 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 Share by email 
 -->
 STAR-ADVERTISER / 2023
 High surf is seen on Maui at Peʻahi surf break, also known as Jaws. A high surf advisory and a small craft advisory are in effect today, and a showery tradewind pattern is expected to settle in through much of the week.
 A high surf advisory and a small craft advisory are in effect today, and a showery tradewind pattern is expected to settle in through much of the week.
 The surf advisory is in effect until 6 a.m. Tuesday for the north shores of Maui and the Big Island, the National Weather Service said. Breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet and strong currents will make swimming dangerous. They advised people to follow ocean safety officials’ guidance and to stay out of the water if in doubt.
 Forecasters said a moderate north swell will peak this morning and then slowly decline through Wednesday. Moderate to heavy surges are expected in north-facing harbors, especially Kahului Harbor on Maui and Hilo Harbor on the Big Island. Boaters should use caution when mooring, launching and entering or leaving port.
 A small craft advisory is in effect for all Hawaiian waters until 6 a.m. Tuesday. East winds of about 17 to 29 mph and seas of 7 to 11 feet are forecast around Kauai, Oahu, Maui County and the Big Island’s windward waters. Winds of about 23 to 35 mph and seas of 7 to 12 feet are forecast for Kaiwi Channel, Maalaea Bay, Pailolo Channel, Alenuihaha Channel and the Big Island’s leeward and southeast waters.
 The advisory will likely be extended for those waters, according to weather officials. They said winds and seas should gradually lower, with the advisory likely scaling back to the typically windy waters around Maui and the Big Island late Tuesday or Wednesday.
 Showers are expected to increase across the state this afternoon through Tuesday morning, mostly on windward and mauka areas, forecasters said. A band of clouds left over from a front is moving toward the islands and will ride up island mountains on the tradewinds. Rainfall is forecast to be light to moderate.

 Forecasters said the wet tradewind pattern should last through much of the week and into the weekend. A weak area of low pressure high in the atmosphere is expected to drift across the islands Wednesday and Thursday, and another band of clouds is expected Friday. The highest rainfall totals are forecast along windward mountain areas, with lower totals on drier leeward sides.
 Breezy tradewinds of 15 to 25 mph are expected to ease to 15 to 20 mph Tuesday and Wednesday. Winds are forecast to strengthen late Thursday into Friday, reaching 15 to 30 mph from the east across Kauai, Oahu and Maui County. Forecasters said lower winds, higher humidity and more showers should limit critical fire weather conditions through Thursday.
